the SAMS and SWWB were weaker than today during the last deglacial, while the SAMS was stronger than today during the entire Holocene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of the changing impact of two major climatic systems on sediment composition at a key area off SE South America during the last 14000 years.

the reconstruction of the meridional migration of the STSF and BMC and their influence on the sediment distribution and composition of SE South America during the last 13.8–11.7 cal kyr and the Late Glacial–Holocene transition (11.7–11.0 cal kyr).

the first quantitative reconstruction of the impact of the SWWB and the SAMS on sediment composition at a specific site of the SE South America continental shelf, which is under the control of both climatic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the modern climatic conditions of the SAMS, the SWWB and the STSF are a Late Holocene phenomenon.

the SAMS and SWWB are in a state of dynamic equilibrium with the Southern Hemisphere's ocean-atmospheric system, and their meridional positions are controlled by the strength of the Southern Hemisphere's westerlies.
the SWWB and the SAMS are not in phase, but the SAMS is the dominant climatic system in this region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SAMS and SWWB were in an opposite phase during most of the Holocene.

the modern climatic situation over SE South America has developed gradually during the last 13 cal kyr, and the Rio Grande Cone off SE Brazil is an ideal site for the reconstruction of this climatic development.
the SAMS and SWWB were not in equilibrium during the last deglaciation, which is also supported by other paleoclimatic proxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SAMS and SWWB are not only the major drivers of modern oceanographic conditions at the SE South American margin but also the key factors that determine the sediment distribution of this region during the last 20 ka.

the SAMS and SWWB were in phase with the South American Summer Monsoon System during the Late Glacial, Early Holocene, and Late Holocene and in phase with the Southern Hemisphere Westerly Wind System during the Mid Holocene.
both climatic systems have a strong impact on the meridional positions of the STSF and BMC.
